column1: # Measured seconds per shell suite and node file, read by tests/lib/shard.py (its docstring holds the format and the
# rules): each entry's load in the full suite's shard split (ADR 0073 d3), so the shards balance on time, not file size,
# and node's order (shard.py --order: tests/run.sh starts node's files longest first, p54-3).
# tests/run.sh reads it too, for each shell suite's liveness bound (tests/lib/test-jobs.sh's suite_bounds): 12x the weight
# rounded up, at least 300 s, 1200 s for a suite with none. In master's full-suite.yml macOS shards from
# 2026-11-16T15:00Z to 2026-11-19, macOS CI ran a suite at up to 9.2x these local seconds in the runs it finished
# (skills/execute/tests/reconcile-rollout-standing.test.sh, 271 s against its measured 29.5), and at about 12x and 8x in
# the runs that cut two suites at their bounds (master's shard 3/4, 2026-11-17 to 18), so those three rows hold floors,
# below. A suite whose seconds grow towards its bound needs this file regenerated, or it is killed as hung.
# Source: the per-suite `<label>: ok (<N>s)` lines of two local `make test` runs (2026-11-19, p49-1, on master at
# 9dd298d), at the default cap of 4 on a 12-core Mac, load 9 to 15 under other rollouts; each value is the median of
# the two. @merge-task-self-tests is its two self-tests summed. A suite that ended within its first second (0 s) is
# written as 0.5, since a weight must be positive.
# Node files (*.mjs, p54-3): the `<seconds><TAB><file>` lines of the `== node seconds per file` block that
# tests/lib/node-run.mjs prints at the end of node's phase (each file's top-level tests' duration_ms summed), from the
# same two runs, the median of the two; a file under 0.1 s is written as 0.1.
# Regenerate: run `make test` twice, take each suite's median from those lines and each node file's from that block,
# sum the two self-tests, and rewrite this file whole, keeping the three floored rows below at least as high. A suite or
# node file added since falls back to its size times the median seconds per byte of its kind (shard.py).
# Three rows hold floors, sized from macOS CI because their measured seconds give a bound under 1.5x a CI time; a row
# whose measured seconds pass its floor is written at them. A cut run's full time is its cut seconds over the share of a
# lone local run's time its last check had reached (`bash <suite>` with each line timed).
# - skills/execute/tests/reconcile-rollout-queue.test.sh is 67. Its `make test` lines read 46 and 46 (44 and 44 on
#   342, 32.8 s into a 49.2 s local run (two thirds), so that run would have taken about 535 s, 12x the 44. 67 gives an
#   804 s bound, 1.5x that; 46 gives 552 s, 1.03x, and CI would cut it again.
# - tests/fast-tier.test.sh's floor is 86, and its `make test` lines read 87 and 91, so it is written at 89 (84 and 83
#   44233636618) cut it at 300 s after its R8 and R10, 36.6 and 40.7 s into an 82.9 s local run, so those runs would
#   have taken about 680 and 610 s, 8x the 84. 86 gives a 1032 s bound, 1.5x the 680 s; 89 gives 1068 s.
# - skills/execute/tests/reconcile-rollout-standing.test.sh is 34. Its `make test` lines read 29 and 30. Job
#   133719463294 (run 43987540320) passed it at 271 s, 9.2x the 29.5 and 4x its 69 s median in that window. 34 gives a
#   408 s bound, 1.5x the 271 s; 29.5 gives 354 s, 1.31x, and one slower run would be killed as hung.
# A regenerate keeps each at least that high until macOS CI passes them well under their bounds: written back below
# their floors, they fail tests/test-jobs.test.sh's ci_max guard, which holds the same 535, 680 and 271 s.
# ---- node files (p54-3) ----
